newsitem.title: USA: Whitewater prosecutor seeks different judge.
newsitem.headline: Whitewater prosecutor seeks different judge.

text.p: - A federal judge who postponed a trial in the Whitewater investigation should reverse his decision and allow another judge to study the issue, the Whitewater special prosecutor said Friday.
In a motion employing unusually terse language, special prosecutor Kenneth Starr said the judge had erred in postponing indefinately the bankruptcy fraud trial of former Arkansas Gov. Jim Guy Tucker.

Starr said the judge was biased toward a doctor who claimed Tucker was physically unable to withstand a trial, which was scheduled for September. The judge had acknowledged in his order that he had been a patient of the doctor's.

"Due to the Court's personal relationship with one of Mr. Tucker's physicians and its acknowledged unwillingness even to entertain contrary views, it is incumbent upon the Court to refer this issue to another judge for prompt resolution," said the special prosecutor's motion, which Starr signed.

On Tuesday, U.S. District Judge Stephen Reasoner granted a defence motion and postponed Tucker's trial, denying Starr a hearing on the issue. Reasoner said the doctor, C. Don Greenway of Little Rock, had an "unsurpassed" reputation and that any evidence the special prosecutor might present regarding Tucker's ability to stand trial would not likely be persuasive.
But Starr said: "The evidence presented by Mr. Tucker does not even approach the standard of proof required" to prove physical inability to withstand a trial.

Starr said that a different judge should study the issue of a postponement given "this Court's candid admission of its partiality towards a defence witness and its stated intent to credit his testimony over any evidence the United States might present."

Tucker and two other men are charged with attempting to defraud the government in the sale of a cable television system more than a decade ago. Starr claimed jurisdiction in the case because, he has said, he uncovered the alleged offences in the course of his investigation of the personal and political finances of President and Mrs. Clinton.

It would be Tucker's second trial in a case brought by Starr. In 1996, Tucker was convicted of fraud and conspiracy along with Clinton's former partners in the Whitewater real estate project, James McDougal and his former wife, Susan McDougal.
Both McDougals are in prison. Tucker was sentenced to home detention because of failing health and last December received a liver transplant.
